ai.literal: Many to dislike, benefit things-without he who speaks, everyone to mock will experience.
ai.translation: He who speaks useless words to the disgust of many will be despised by everyone.
ai.modern: பலரும் வெறுக்கும்படி பயனில்லாத சொற்களைச் சொல்பவன், எல்லாராலும் இகழப்படுவான்.
ai.explanation: This couplet warns against speaking words that serve no purpose. When a person speaks uselessly, it annoys and disgusts the many people listening. Consequently, that person will lose respect and be mocked by everyone. The word 'முனிய' means to dislike or be disgusted, showing the immediate reaction of the listeners, while 'எள்ள' means to mock or despise, showing the lasting loss of respect.

ai.literal: Benefit without-things many-people before speaking, goodness without-things friends-at than-doing is-bad.
ai.translation: Speaking useless words in front of a crowd is worse than doing unkind deeds to one's own friends.
ai.modern: பலருக்கு முன்னே பயனில்லாத சொற்களைச் சொல்வது, நண்பர்களுக்கு இனிமையற்ற செயல்களைச் செய்வதை விடத் தீமையானது.
ai.explanation: This couplet emphasizes the harm of speaking uselessly in public. The poet compares it to acting unkindly towards close friends, which is already a severe wrong. By stating that public babbling is even worse than such betrayal, the verse strongly warns against wasting words and the time of others. The word 'நயன்' refers to goodness or pleasantness, contrasting with the uselessness of 'பயன் இல'.

ai.literal: goodness he-is-without the-fact-that will-declare use things-without having-elaborated which-speaks speech
ai.translation: A speech that elaborately dwells on useless things will declare that the speaker is a man without goodness.
ai.modern: பயனில்லாத சொற்களை விரிவாகப் பேசும் ஒருவனது பேச்சே, அவன் அறம் இல்லாதவன் என்பதை உலகிற்குச் சொல்லிவிடும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet explains how useless speech exposes a person's true character. When someone speaks at length about things that have no purpose or benefit, their own words act as a witness against them. The very act of elaborating on useless topics clearly declares to others that the speaker lacks inner goodness and virtue.

ai.literal: Fairness not-conforming-to, from goodness will-remove, usefulness lacking quality-without word many-people in-presence.
ai.translation: Speaking useless, uncultured words in the presence of many people will distance the speaker from fairness and strip away their goodness.
ai.modern: பலருக்கு முன்னே பயனில்லாத பண்பற்ற சொற்களைச் சொல்வது, ஒருவனை நீதியோடு சேரவிடாமல் அவனுடைய நன்மையிலிருந்தும் நீக்கிவிடும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet warns against speaking useless and uncultured words in a public gathering. Such speech lacks any meaningful purpose and shows a lack of good character. Consequently, it alienates the speaker from fairness and destroys their inherent goodness. The repetition of the word 'சாரா' (not conforming or lacking) emphasizes how such words are entirely disconnected from both justice and utility.

ai.literal: Greatness with eminence will depart, useless things, good-nature possessors if speak.
ai.translation: If people of good nature speak useless words, their greatness and eminence will depart from them.
ai.modern: நல்ல பண்புகளை உடையவர்கள் பயனில்லாத சொற்களைப் பேசினால், அவர்களுடைய பெருமையும் சிறப்பும் அவர்களை விட்டு நீங்கிவிடும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet warns about the consequences of speaking useless words for people of good character. The phrase 'நீர்மை உடையார்' refers to those who possess a naturally good and noble disposition. If such people speak 'பயன் இல' (words without use or benefit), the text states that their inherent greatness along with their special social esteem will depart from them. The verb 'நீங்கும்' (will depart) emphasizes that respect and dignity are not permanent, but depend on the continuous exercise of meaningful speech.

ai.literal: Him who dwells upon words without benefit, calling a man [is wrong]; calling the chaff of people [is right].
ai.translation: Do not call a person a man if he dwells upon useless words; call him the chaff among human beings.
ai.modern: பயனில்லாத சொற்களைத் திரும்பத் திரும்பப் பேசுபவனை ஒரு மனிதன் என்று சொல்லக்கூடாது; அவனை மனிதர்களுள் பதர் என்றுதான் சொல்ல வேண்டும்.
ai.explanation: The couplet strongly condemns the habit of speaking useless words. The word 'பாராட்டுவானை' refers to someone who repeatedly dwells upon or celebrates empty talk. The poet uses the word 'எனல்' (a verbal noun meaning saying or calling) twice to create a sharp contrast, functioning as an injunction. Calling such a person a 'மகன்' (a true human being) is wrong; instead, one should call him 'பதடி' (chaff), the empty husk of grain that has no substance or value among people.

ai.literal: Pleasantness things without even if they speak let them speak the noble ones; usefulness things without not speaking is good.
ai.translation: Even if the noble speak words lacking pleasantness, let them speak; but it is good that they do not speak words lacking usefulness.
ai.modern: சான்றோர்கள் இனிமை இல்லாத சொற்களைச் சொன்னாலும் சொல்லலாம், ஆனால் பயன் இல்லாத சொற்களைச் சொல்லாமல் இருப்பதே அவர்களுக்குச் சிறந்தது.
ai.explanation: This couplet contrasts words lacking pleasantness with words lacking usefulness. It states that even if noble people happen to speak harsh or unpleasant words, it can be tolerated. However, it is essential and truly good that they refrain entirely from speaking useless words. The emphasis is on the absolute avoidance of vain talk by the wise.

ai.translation: The wise, who seek out rare and meaningful benefits, will not speak words that lack great purpose.

ai.explanation: This couplet emphasizes the careful speech of the truly wise. The word 'அரும்பயன்' refers to rare, profound benefits that wise people constantly seek and analyze. Because their minds are focused on such valuable pursuits, they naturally avoid trivialities. Therefore, they will never utter words that do not yield a substantial, great benefit.

ai.literal: Meaning devoid-of, even forgetting they will not speak, delusion freed-from, blemish without vision-they.
ai.translation: Those of flawless vision, freed from delusion, will not speak meaningless words even in a moment of forgetfulness.
ai.modern: மயக்கம் நீங்கிய குற்றமற்ற அறிவை உடையவர்கள், மறந்துபோய்க்கூடப் பயனில்லாத சொற்களைச் சொல்ல மாட்டார்கள்.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the deep discipline of the wise regarding their speech. The phrase 'மருள் தீர்ந்த மாசறு காட்சியவர்' describes individuals whose understanding is perfectly clear, completely free from confusion and flaws. Because their minds are so pure, they will not utter words devoid of substance ('பொருள் தீர்ந்த'), even in a careless moment of forgetfulness ('பொச்சாந்தும்'). It shows that speaking purposefully is an unbreakable habit for those with true clarity.

ai.literal: Speak, if speaking, (things) possessing benefit; do not speak, if speaking, word(s) without benefit.
ai.translation: If you speak, speak words that yield some benefit. If you speak, never speak words that are useless.
ai.modern: பேசினால் பயன்தரும் சொற்களையே பேசவேண்டும்; பேசும்போது பயனில்லாத சொற்களைப் பேசவே கூடாது.
ai.explanation: This couplet provides a clear rule for communication: every spoken word should serve a purpose. The word 'சொல்லில்' (if speaking) is repeated to emphasize that the act of speaking is a deliberate choice. By contrasting 'பயனுடைய' (possessing benefit) with 'பயனிலா' (without benefit), the text urges the learner to consciously filter their speech, ensuring that only meaningful words are uttered while useless ones are withheld.
